lex.uz: hukmronlik qilib, tabiiy deb qabul qilingan

grammar.label: code-switching and the multilingual sentence
grammar.form: switching language at a clause boundary, for a quotation, a term or an identity
grammar.meaning: moves between languages in a way both speakers accept

explanation.en: Switching languages mid-sentence is rule-governed, not random: it happens at clause boundaries, at borrowed terms with no equivalent, and at moments of identity. A bilingual audience reads it as fluent; a monolingual one reads it as showing off. The skill is knowing which room you are in.
explanation.uz: Til almashtirish tasodifiy emas, qoidaga bo'ysunadi: gap chegarasida, ekvivalenti yo'q atamada va o'zlikni ko'rsatish onida. Ikki tilli auditoriya buni ravonlik deb o'qiydi.

grammar.positive_example: She used the Uzbek term and glossed it once, because the audience was mixed.
grammar.negative_example: She used the Uzbek term throughout and glossed it in a footnote nobody read.

l1_notes.uz: Ikki tilli nutqda til almashtirish tabiiy; bir tilli auditoriyada u boshqacha o'qiladi.

grammar.label: the English of somewhere else — varieties as systems
grammar.form: Indian, Nigerian, Singaporean and Caribbean standard forms with their own rules
grammar.meaning: recognises a variety as a system rather than as an error

explanation.en: 'I am having three brothers' is standard Indian English and follows a rule — stative verbs take the progressive there. It is not a mistake any more than American 'gotten' is. At C2 the question is never whether a form is correct but in which standard, and whether your reader shares it.
explanation.uz: 'I am having three brothers' — Hind ingliz tilining me'yori va qoidaga bo'ysunadi. Bu xato emas, xuddi amerikacha 'gotten' xato bo'lmagani kabi.

grammar.positive_example: The form is standard in Indian English and follows a consistent rule.
grammar.negative_example: The form is a common Indian English error caused by the local language.

l1_notes.uz: Ingliz tilining ko'p me'yori borligi — C2 darajadagi asosiy tushuncha; maktab ta'limi odatda bittasini o'rgatadi.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: A teacher sent me this and asked me to mark it wrong.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: In America that is ordinary and correct. Here it is marked as an error every single time.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So what do I tell a student in Tashkent?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That the examination is marked against one variety, that the sentence is not wrong in itself, and that those are two separate facts.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: They will ask which English is the correct one.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Ask them which Uzbek is correct, the one in Khiva or the one in Andijan.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Nobody asks it about their own language, which tells you the question was never really about language.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Bobur puts three borrowed words in every Uzbek sentence.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And every one of them is doing a job the other language does faster. He is not being lazy. He switches where the grammar lets him and nowhere else.
